questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Existentialism has a reputation for being angst-ridden and gloomy mostly because of its emphasis on pondering the meaningless of existence.

options.text: on pondering the meaningless of existence

questions.solution:
The erroneous sentence is: **on pondering the meaningless of existence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the word 'meaningless' is incorrect and should be replaced with 'meaninglessness'.
 
• The correct form should be *pondering the meaninglessness of existence*.
 
• The presence of article **'the'** before **'meaningless' **hints at the fact that the **word **must be replaced by a **noun (meaninglessness) **as **'meaningless' **is an **adjective**.
 
• This is because** 'meaninglessness'** is the noun form that correctly fits the context of the sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *Existentialism has a reputation for being angst-ridden and gloomy mostly because of its emphasis on pondering the **meaninglessness **of existence*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word **'meaningless'** is an **adjective**, and in the given context, a noun form is required.
 
• Adjectives describe nouns, but in this case, we need a noun to describe the state of having no meaning.
 
• Therefore, 'meaninglessness' is the correct noun form to use in this context.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

To __preparing the vine for plant__, it should be cut back to 2 ft.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **prepare the vine for planting**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The original sentence has a grammatical error in verb tense and usage. "To preparing" should be corrected to "To prepare".
 
• **"Prepare the vine for planting"** correctly expresses the action of getting the vine ready for planting.
 
• The phrase **"to prepare"** functions as an **infinitive verb form**, which is used to express purpose or intention.
 
• **"The vine" **is the direct object of the infinitive verb **"to prepare".** This construction correctly identifies what is being prepared.
 
• **"For planting"** is a **prepositional phrase** that modifies the infinitive verb **"to prepare"**. It specifies the purpose or destination of the preparation action.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is - **Option 4**.

The correct sentence is: *To **prepare the vine for planting**__, it should be cut back to 2 ft.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

The student provided her English teacher a short and _________(incoherent) account of her journey to Shimla with her parents.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **lucid.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"incoherent"** means something that is unclear, confusing, or not logically connected. (अस्पष्ट)

 
 
• **Example: **His speech was incoherent, making it hard for anyone to understand his point.
 
 
 
• **"Lucid"** refers to something that is clear and easy to understand; it is logically connected and well-organized. (स्पष्ट)
 
 
• **Example: **The professor provided a lucid explanation of the complex theory, making it easy for students to grasp.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'incoherent'** is **'lucid'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. lucid**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Humble** (विनम्र): Having or showing a modest or low estimate of one's importance.

 
 
• **Example:** Despite his success, he remained humble and approachable.
 
 
 
• **Rough** (खुरदरा): Having an uneven or irregular surface; not smooth.
 
 
• **Example:** The rough texture of the wall made it difficult to paint.
 
 
 
• **Genuine** (असली): Truly what something is said to be; authentic.
 
 
• **Example:** She wore a genuine smile that brightened up the room.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I want to / give you / an information about / the missing necklace.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **an information about**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase 'an information about' is incorrect because 'information' is an **uncountable noun **and should not be preceded by the article 'an'.
 
• Instead, it should be 'some information about' or simply 'information about'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *I want to give you **some information** about the missing necklace*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Uncountable nouns like 'information', 'advice', 'equipment', etc., should not be used with articles like 'a' or 'an'.
 
• Instead, use quantifiers like 'some', 'any', or phrases like 'a piece of'.

By living in a rural area with access to the city, she gets _____.

• **Example:** By working part-time, she gets the best of both worlds - time with her kids and a career.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

• **Example:** She always keeps an ear to the ground to know about the latest fashion trends.
 
 
 
• **On cloud nine **(बहुत खुश): To be extremely happy.
 
 
• **Example:** She was on cloud nine after winning the competition.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.

The conductor said that it was the __worse__ quake he ever knew.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **worst**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the word "worse" is incorrect when comparing it to past experiences of the conductor.
 
• Instead, the superlative form "worst" should be used to indicate that this earthquake was the most severe one the conductor had ever experienced.
 
• Superlative adjectives are used to describe an object which is at the upper or lower limit of a quality (e.g., the tallest, the smallest, the fastest, the highest).
 
• The sentence should read: "*The conductor said that it was the worst quake he ever knew.*"

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *The conductor said that it was the worst quake he ever knew.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When comparing two objects, use the comparative form of the adjective (e.g., better, worse).
 
• When comparing more than two objects, use the superlative form of the adjective (e.g., best, worst).
 
• Examples:
 
 
• *This is the best book I have ever read.*
 
• *Out of the three runners, she is the fastest.*
